text:
Maya: Heads-up — pinto-v0.9 (int8) onboard canary trending worse on structured-output checks vs fp16. Quick numbers from nightly eval: schema_adherence dropped from 94.1% -> 88.2%, malformed-field rate 0.8% -> 3.9% :thinking:

Maya: sample bad output:
```json
{"req_id":"abc123","response":{"items":[{"id":"1","label":"apple"},{"id":2,"label":null}],"meta": {"confidence":"0.92"}}
```

Zheng: hmm that second item has id as int and label null — schema expects strings for both. Any streaming/truncation happening?

Olin: were you running with prefix cache + batching? those have weird interactions with quantized kernels sometimes. Try disabling prefix cache and batch=1.

Maya: canary command we used:
```bash
run_canary --model=pinto-v0.9 --quant=int8 --batch=8 --prefix-cache=true --dataset=structured-evals/slice-A
```

Eval-bot: Snapshot: schema_adherence: "94.1% -> 88.2%", parse_fail_rate: "0.8% -> 3.9%", avg_latency: "142ms -> 131ms" (int8 faster, but correctness regressed)

Sre-jay: also double-check tokenizer version + BPE vocab on the canary node. Tokenization drift can silently change sampling offsets.

Zheng: quick experiments I'd run: (A) int8 + bias-corr/zero-point fix; (B) int8 + prefix-cache=false + batch=1; (C) fp16 replica to confirm baseline. If (B) fixes it then it's likely a kv-prefix or batching kernel interaction.

Maya: proposed plan:
1) kick off experiment B over 2k samples, batch=1, prefix-cache=false
2) if malformed rate > 1.5% after run, rollback canary to fp16 and open regression ticket with failing examples
3) collect tokenized traces + logits for failing cases and attach to ticket for model-runtime triage

Olin: +1. Add /eval tag and push the experiment metrics to the structured-output dashboard (https://dash/internal/struct-adhesion). Also add a small smoke test in the canary job to catch this next time.

Maya: starting experiment B now, ETA ~45m. Will drop results and a failing sample pack here when done. :rocket:
